Stossel: What are libertarians doing wrong?

I think one of the biggest problems for the libertarians is voters' attitudes. Many people refuse to "waste their vote" by voting third-party. This morning I was talking to a man in my sociology class and I asked why he didn't support Gary Johnson. He replied that he wasn't willing to vote for him because he had no chance of winning. I feel bad about this because it becomes a cycle that libertarians and independents can't escape: Nobody votes for them because they're not viable; they're not viable because they get few votes. Even if they're good candidates, it doesn't matter.

I disagree with the notion that I'm wasting my vote by voting libertarian, because if lots of people started voting libertarian, it sends a signal to the two big parties to move in a more libertarian direction. Then, if the Democrats or Republicans run someone who is somewhat libertarian, I'll vote for them. I don't vote strictly based on party; I'll vote for anyone who wants to decrease the size and intrusiveness of government, even if it's just by a little. I'm a radical libertarian, but I think moderate libertarians are a step in the right direction, and any reduction in tyranny, no matter how small, is a great thing these days.
Wasted Vote Syndrome isn't a Syndrome. It's a plague.
